svg.title: Four Pre-Flight Checks Before Accepting Orders
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-product-and-order-preflight; chart type: decision_tree; title: Four Pre-Flight Checks Before Accepting Orders; subtitle: Resolve product, customs, tax, and customer-treatment risks.; chapter number: 5; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: Four sequential yes-or-no checks; numeric values indicate sequence only. A documented pass advances to the next check. A failed check follows the corrective branch described in its detail; product category and jurisdiction determine scope.; caption: Use written evidence rather than a single vendor assurance. After all four checks pass, release only the affected, documented products and selling destinations.; stages: label: Check product safety and supplier traceability; value: Check 1: pass documented safety and sourcing requirements; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Confirm dealer authorization, applicable testing and certificates, and recall screening. Under 15 U.S.C. 2064, evaluate immediate reporting duties when hazard information arises. Failure routes affected stock to quarantine and review.; label: Check customs classification and landed import cost; value: Check 2: pass importer and duty documentation; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Identify the importer of record and verify HTS classification, origin, and applicable duties under 19 U.S.C. 1484. For domestic purchases, retain supplier invoices and responsibility records. Failure pauses affected purchasing.; label: Check sales-tax nexus and collection configuration; value: Check 3: pass destination-specific tax setup verification; numeric value: 3.0; detail: Review economic and physical nexus, including 3PL-held inventory. California Revenue and Taxation Code Section 6203 illustrates state-specific triggers. Separate marketplace collection from direct-store duties; unresolved destinations remain disabled.; label: Check promises, privacy, and retention messaging; value: Check 4: pass customer-facing workflow verification; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Test shipping promises and delay handling under 16 CFR Part 435, claims under 15 U.S.C. 45, email opt-outs under 15 U.S.C. 7704, and applicable California Civil Code 1798.100 duties. Failure pauses the affected offer or flow until corrected and retested.
